prompt:
A line-art multi-panel storyboard of one continuous scene of a live-action short drama: one image divided into a grid of 4 columns and 4 rows of equal 9:16 panels, 13 panels read from left to right and top to bottom; cells after the last panel stay plain white. Every panel is a clean, simple line drawing: uniform thin black outlines on a plain white background, with no shading, hatching, grey tones, colour or texture. Each panel has a thin black border, with plain white gutters between the panels. Location: The Quinn family mansion, living room, Day, bright daylight through the arched French windows, warm chandelier fill.
Image 1: the character sheet of Natalie (25), look S0
Image 2: the character sheet of George (55), look S0
Image 3: the character sheet of Lauren (50), look S0
Image 4: the location The Quinn family mansion, living room, the front view, the establishing view, facing the back wall, with no people
Image 5: the location The Quinn family mansion, living room, the back view, turned 180 degrees, facing the front wall, with the left wall at its right edge, with no people
Image 6: the location The Quinn family mansion, living room, the left-side view, facing the left wall, with the back wall at its right edge, with no people
Image 7: the location The Quinn family mansion, living room, the right-side view, facing the right wall, with the back wall at its left edge, with no people
Image 8: the location The Quinn family mansion, living room, the floor plan seen from above: its top edge is the back wall, its bottom edge the front wall behind the front view's camera, and its left and right edges the left and right walls, with no people
Image 9: the blocking reference of this segment, the same place with its people in their places at the start; use it only for where each person is and which way they face, and keep each person on that seat or spot, on the same side of the room, in every panel until a shot moves them; do not copy its colours or light
Image 10: the prop hospital statement; use only structure, material, and color
Draw each character so they can be told apart as in their reference image: the hairstyle, build and outfit in outline. Use the character sheets only for the characters, not for their layout, white background or multiple views. Use the location images only for the layout of the space and the place of its furniture and props, drawn in outline. There is only one of each vehicle, piece of furniture and prop that the location shows, defined by the location images, throughout all panels; when a panel shows only part of one, such as a car's hood, it is that same object, and no second one appears. Each panel shows only the characters it names, and nobody appears twice in one panel.
At the start: Axis: the line from the single cream armchair to the long cream sofa. The camera stays on the front (bookshelf) wall side and looks toward the three tall arched French windows on the back wall; reverse singles on Natalie look toward the bookshelf wall. The one long cream sofa runs across the frame in front of the windows and faces the camera. The white marble fireplace is on the left wall at frame left. The open white double doorway is on the right wall at frame right. The one single cream armchair stands in the foreground centre with its back to the camera, facing the sofa across the one low glass-and-gold coffee table. Natalie sits upright in the armchair, three-quarter back to the camera, facing the sofa, hands in her lap. George sits at the fireplace end of the sofa, frame left, facing the camera and Natalie. Lauren sits at the doorway end of the sofa, frame right, at the same depth as George, legs crossed, facing Natalie. The one hospital statement lies flat on the coffee table. Cassie is not yet in the room; she waits out of sight in the marble entrance hall beyond the double doorway.
Panel 1: Wide shot, slow push in from the bookshelf wall toward the sofa, eye-level, symmetrical composition. The cream-and-gold living room in daylight. Natalie sits in the armchair in the foreground centre with her back to the camera. George sits at frame left and Lauren at frame right on the cream sofa in front of the arched windows, with the glass coffee table between them and Natalie.
Panel 2: Close-up insert, locked-off camera, high angle onto the coffee table. The hospital statement lies on the glass coffee table, its bold total at the bottom.
Panel 3: Medium shot, reverse over-the-shoulder shot from behind Lauren's shoulder at the doorway end of the sofa, looking toward the bookshelf wall, eye-level. Lauren's shoulder and hair fill the foreground edge. Natalie in the armchair leans slightly forward toward her father, hands clasped, eyes hopeful.
Panel 4: Medium close-up, reverse clean single on Natalie looking toward the bookshelf wall, locked-off camera, eye-level. Only Natalie, framed tight on her face and shoulders; her eyes glisten as she pleads.
Panel 5: Medium shot, two-shot of the sofa from the front, eye-level. George at the fireplace end of the sofa, frame left, rubs his hands together and glances right at Lauren beside him at frame right.
Panel 6: Medium shot from the front, dirty single on Lauren with George's shoulder at the frame-left edge, slight low angle. Lauren uncrosses her legs and fixes Natalie, toward the camera, with a cold stare, lip curled.
Panel 7: Medium shot, handheld, reverse single on Natalie in the armchair, looking toward the bookshelf wall. Natalie presses a hand to her chest and nods quickly toward the sofa.
Panel 8: Medium shot, two-shot of the sofa from the front, slow push in on George at frame left. George turns right toward Lauren and lifts an open palm, gently placating.
Panel 9: Medium shot, reverse clean single on Natalie looking toward the bookshelf wall, locked-off camera. Only Natalie in the armchair; she looks up toward her father on the sofa, off screen, lips parting with a small flicker of hope.
Panel 10: Close-up from the front, clean single on Lauren, eye-level. Only Lauren, framed tight on her face; her arched brows narrow as she turns her head sharply left toward George.
Panel 11: Medium shot from the front, dirty single on George with Lauren's shoulder at the frame-right edge. George shakes his head quickly and raises both hands.
Panel 12: Medium shot, two-shot of the sofa from the front, slightly above. Lauren at frame right leans left over George and taps a finger against his chest; George at frame left shrinks back into the sofa.
Panel 13: Close-up from the front, clean single on George, locked-off camera. Only George, framed tight on his face and hands; he lowers his eyes and turns his wedding band with his thumb.
Keep the characters, the number and position of every vehicle, piece of furniture and prop, and the location's spatial orientation consistent across all panels.
No text, letters, numbers, captions, speech bubbles, panel labels or watermark anywhere in the image; no photographic rendering, shading or colour.
